title: Prediction of high-risk factor in early-stage lung cancer: micropapillary adenocarcinoma

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Prediction of high-risk factor in early-stage lung cancer: micropapillary adenocarcinoma》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · S0001-p1】Micropapillary lung adenocarcinoma (MPA) is an aggressive histological subtype of invasive lung adenocarcinoma (LADC), characterized by a high propensity for lymphovascular invasion, distant dissemination, and early metastasis. Compared to well-differentiated (lepidic) and moderately differentiated (papillary or acinar) subtypes, MPA is associated with significantly poorer prognosis and increased recurrence risk even in early-stage disease [1]. Although MPA accounts for a relatively small proportion of LADCs, numerous studies have demonstrated that the presence of an MPA component is independently associated with worse clinical outcomes [2–4]. A study has found that MPA is a significant predictor of postoperative brain metastasis in patients with resected lung adenocarcinoma [5]. Even among patients with stage I lung adenocarcinoma, the 5-year overall survival rate for patients with MPA present ranges from 54% to 79%, compared to 73% to 98% in those without MPA involvement [6–13]. These findings underscore the clinical importance of accurate identification of MPA, particularly in early-stage disease, to optimize surgical and adjuvant management strategies.

【Introduction · S0001-p2】Histopathological examination of tissue specimens remains the gold standard for subtype classification in LADC. However, the sensitivity of intraoperative frozen section analysis for detecting MPA is limited to approximately 37%, primarily due to inconsistencies between frozen and formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) sections [14]. Therefore, reliable preoperative prediction of MPA presence holds significant clinical value, as it enables more precise pathological classification and supports individualized treatment planning.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Prediction of high-risk factor in early-stage lung cancer: micropapillary adenocarcinoma》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Patient inclusion · S0002-S2001-p1】This study was approved by the Biomedical Ethics Committee of West China Hospital, Sichuan University. Patients who were pathologically diagnosed with LUAD at West China Hospital between January 2011 and June 2022 were included. To address the classification of patients, two experienced pathologists, each with over 10 years of diagnostic experience, independently reviewed all pathological slides. Based on the presence or absence of a micropapillary component (Supplementary Figure 1) in the tumor sections, patients were divided into the MPA group and the non-MPA group. In cases of disagreement, a senior pathologist with greater experience participated in the review, and the final classification was determined by consensus among the three pathologists. As solid adenocarcinoma is also considered a poorly differentiated, high-grade subtype of adenocarcinoma, cases with a solid component were excluded. Consequently, the pathological subtypes of patients in the non-MPA group included any combination of lepidic, acinar, and papillary patterns. Exclusion criteria were as follows: (1) Pathological stage II-IV disease; (2) Presence of other concurrent malignancies; (3) No surgical specimens; (4) Presence of other poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma components (e.g. solid, mucinous); (5) Diagnosis of multiple primary lung cancers; and (6) Incomplete or missing key clinical data.

【Data collection and processing · S0002-S2002-p1】Due to the significant disparity in patient numbers between the MPA and non-MPA groups, age and gender matching was conducted to establish a more consistent baseline across both groups. This matching procedure aimed to achieve an equal ratio of patients in the MPA group to those in the non-MPA group, set at 1:1. Clinical characteristics, pathological information, imaging data, treatment, and prognosis of patients in the two groups were collected and analyzed, respectively.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Prediction of high-risk factor in early-stage lung cancer: micropapillary adenocarcinoma》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Construction and validation of a non-invasive MPA prediction model and nomogram · S0003-S2003-S3002-p3】To facilitate clinical application, we presented a nomogram to estimate the individualized probability of MPA (Figure 3(A)). Besides, we have developed an online risk calculator to facilitate rapid preoperative estimation of MPA, which integrates the predictors from our nomogram into an interactive web-based tool. The calculator is publicly accessible at: https://mpariskassessment.shinyapps.io/MPA-risk-prediction/. Each predictor – including smoking, CT-diameter, density, lobulation, spiculation, vacuoles and VDT – is assigned a specific number of points according to its relative contribution in the multivariable logistic regression model. By summing the points for all variables, a total score is obtained, which corresponds to the predicted probability of MPA on the bottom scale. Higher total scores indicate a greater likelihood of MPA. To assess the calibration of the nomogram, we constructed a bootstrap-corrected calibration curve based on 1,000 resamples. As shown in Figure 3(B), the bias-corrected curve closely overlapped with the ideal reference line across the entire range of predicted probabilities. Furthermore, to evaluate its discriminative capacity, we generated a ROC curve for the nomogram. The model exhibited good discriminatory performance, with an AUC of 0.923(95%CI [0.903,0.944]) (Figure 3(C)). Additionally, in the Hosmer–Lemeshow test, the p-value was 0.1575, indicating good calibration with consistent agreement between the predicted and observed outcomes across risk groups (Supplementary Figure 2). Moreover, decision curve analysis (DCA) further demonstrated that the nomogram provided a higher net clinical benefit across a wide range of threshold probabilities compared with the treat-all and treat-none strategies, supporting its potential clinical utility (Figure 3(D)). In addition, using the Youden index, we selected 48.13% as the optimal cutoff probability for identifying MPA. The corresponding sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and F1-score were 87.35%, 86.18%, 86.34%, 87.20%, and 86.84%, respectively. Finally, we evaluated the consistency of the model across different subgroups (Figure 3(E)). Specifically, the AUCs for predicting MPA in patients with CT-diameter ≤2 cm, >2 cm, smokers, and non-smokers were 0.899, 0.906, 0.928, and 0.917, respectively, indicating stable predictive performance across these subpopulations. Meanwhile, we found that after stratifying patients in our cohort, 39.06% of high-risk patients experienced recurrence within 2 years, whereas all recurrences in the low-risk group occurred more than 2 years after surgery (p = 0.023). No significant differences were observed between high- and low-risk groups in terms of intrathoracic or distant recurrence (p = 0.152); however, high-risk patients were more likely to develop recurrence involving more than two distant sites. To further evaluate the potential role of nomogram-based risk stratification in guiding treatment decisions, we analyzed the impact of different treatment modalities on prognosis across different risk groups. Although no statistically significant differences were observed among the groups, a trend was noted in the high-risk group, in which patients who underwent lobectomy exhibited inferior long-term outcomes compared with those who received sublobar resection (Supplementary Figure 3).

【Results · abstract-3-1】The recurrence rate was significantly higher in the MPA group compared to the non-MPA group. Independent risk factors for MPA included smoking history, CT-diameter (≥22.5 mm), partially-solid nodule (PSN), solid nodule (SN), lobulation, spiculation, presence of vacuoles, and volume doubling time (VDT) (≤310 days). Guided by the multivariable analysis, we constructed a clinically oriented nomogram to provide an intuitive and practical tool for predicting MPA. The nomogram demonstrated excellent discrimination for predicting MPA, with an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.923.
